Cauchy–Schwarz for vectors (a_x,a_Jx) and (a_{x+h},a_{J(x+h)}) gives b_xb_{x+h}≥[a_xa_{x+h}+a_Jx a_J(x+h)]/2. Summation and J(x+h)=Jx−h turn the second term into R_{−h}(a)=R_h(a); squared lengths yield R_0 equality. Strict RMS on any unequal reflection orbit increases Σ a, hence increases Σ_h R_h=(Σ a)² and forces a strict nonzero lag. Orthogonality gives ||Ta||_{2s}^{2s}=Σ_{h_1+...+h_s=0}Π R_{h_j}(a); the term (h,−h,0,...,0), with R_0>0, gives strict improvement for all s≥2. Triangle majorant from convolution handles arbitrary complex phases; finite S gives maximizers by compactness. value.rationale: A single constructive coefficient operation improves every aperiodic/periodic autocorrelation simultaneously, with the exact equality condition and strict improvement of every even moment. This imposes reflected modulus symmetry on maximizers over any centrally symmetric finite frequency mask in any discrete abelian group and reduces their free real amplitude parameters, independent of sharp constants. This is a coherent structural optimization lemma rather than a renamed textbook majorant; the vector Cauchy–Schwarz step alone does not state the simultaneous extremizer consequence.
residual_risks: Does not determine any general sharp synthesis norm or phases; applies only to positive even exponents.

final_claim: On each finite reflection-invariant mask S in a discrete abelian group, pairwise RMS symmetrization of magnitudes preserves the ℓ² norm and increases every autocorrelation, hence every positive even Fourier moment strictly unless the original magnitudes already respect the reflection; every 2s-norm maximizer therefore has reflected equal moduli.
limitations: No claim for non-even exponents or uniqueness of maximizing phases.
Historical equivalent symmetrization may exist outside located indexed literature.
No certified full-text exclusion of Goldstein–McDonald 1984.
